title: Erase coordinated with every writer
notes: Writers run by hand took no lock,
so one active during `atrium erase --apply` could write erased material back. Taking the
refresh lock in the engine would have broken the refresh: `atrium-refresh` holds it through
`atrium-lock` and runs `uv run atrium ingest-synthesis` as a child, whose fresh `flock`
conflicts with its parent's. Design adjudicated with Codex.
result: a new `<state>/erase.lock`. `main` takes it shared and non-blocking for the 14 writing commands (`atrium/erase/writer_commands.py`; `synthesize` unless `--dry-run`, `rekey-synthesis` only with `--apply`) and refuses with exit 3 while an erase holds it. `erase --apply` takes it exclusively before the refresh and synthesis locks, and re-inventories registry files and curation candidates under them. Erased conversation ids go to `<state>/erased-conversations.txt` (fsynced, directory too) before the first delete and stay after: `session-stop` never asks an erased session for a record, and `record-session` consumes its checkpoint without writing. `serve-context` neither saves nor serves a rebuilt dense matrix the index has moved past, and takes back a save that raced an erase. Dispatch moved from `atrium/cli.py` to `atrium/commands/run_command.py`. Not done: the gate is per instance, so a writer pointed with `--index` at another index is still refused during an erase (conservative, by choice).
evidence: `uv run pytest` 582 passed, 2 skipped; `uv run codeality-py gate`, ruff and mypy clean. New tests fail without the change (4 of them checked by reverting it): writer refused under erase, erase refused under a writer, writer runs under a held refresh lock, erased ids kept after completion, erased session consumed and never asked, matrix rebuild overtaken by a delete. Codex reviewed the diff; its two defects (later checkpoints, no directory fsync) are fixed.
